steps.title: Fit new seals and bushings
steps.instruction: Cover the end of the inner tube with a thin plastic bag oiled with fork oil. Slide on a new dust seal, the stopper ring, a new oil seal with its numbered side down, the washer and a new slide metal. Grease the seal lips with lithium grease. Fit a new piston metal into the groove of the inner tube.
verification: New seals and bushings fitted the right way round.

steps.title: Join the tubes
steps.instruction: Oil the inner tube and slide the outer tube on. Drive the slide metal and washer into the outer tube with the fork seal driver (Yamaha 90890-01502), then the oil seal until the stopper ring groove is fully visible. Seat the stopper ring in its groove and press the dust seal home. Slide the tubes: they must move smoothly.

steps.title: Check the locknut position
steps.instruction: Measure from the bottom of the damper to the bottom of the locknut: it must be 16 mm (0.63 in) or more. Turn the locknut to correct it.

steps.title: Fit spring and damper
steps.instruction: Fit the upper spring seat with its larger end toward the spring, and the spring, onto the damper. Lower the damper slowly into the inner tube until it reaches the bottom. Back the rebound adjuster fully out.
verification: Damper sitting on the bottom of the tube.

steps.title: Fit the bottom adjuster
steps.instruction: Fit the damper adjusting rod. Compress the inner tube, set the ring wrench under the locknut and screw the bottom adjuster with a new copper washer onto the rod by hand until it stops. The gap between adjuster and locknut must be 0.5–1.0 mm (0.02–0.04 in); reset the locknut if not. Hold the locknut and tighten the adjuster to 29 Nm (21 lb-ft). Then put threadlocker on the adjuster thread and tighten it into the inner tube to 55 Nm (41 lb-ft).
verification: Adjuster 29 Nm (21 lb-ft) and 55 Nm (41 lb-ft).

steps.title: Fill the outer chamber
steps.instruction: Pour 280 cm³ (9.47 US oz, 9.88 Imp.oz) of Yamaha Suspension Oil S1 into the leg (tuning range 260–365 cm³ (8.79–12.34 US oz, 9.17–12.87 Imp.oz); both legs must match). Thread the cap into the outer tube by hand and fit the protector guide.

steps.title: Fit the legs
steps.instruction: Slide each leg into the brackets and snug the lower pinch bolts. Tighten the cap to 30 Nm (22 lb-ft) with the ring wrench. Set the top of the outer tube 5 mm (0.2 in) above the upper bracket, then tighten the upper pinch bolts to 21 Nm (15 lb-ft) and the lower pinch bolts to 21 Nm (15 lb-ft). Do not overtighten the lower ones: it binds the fork.
verification: Caps 30 Nm (22 lb-ft); pinch bolts 21 Nm (15 lb-ft) / 21 Nm (15 lb-ft).
Top height 5 mm (0.2 in) both sides.

steps.title: Refit protectors, caliper and wheel
steps.instruction: Fit the protectors at 7 Nm (5.2 lb-ft), the caliper at 28 Nm (21 lb-ft) and the brake hose holder. Grease the axle, fit the wheel with the disc between the pads, pump the fork several times and tighten the axle nut to 115 Nm (85 lb-ft), then the pinch bolts to 21 Nm (15 lb-ft). Pump the brake lever until it is firm.
verification: Axle nut 115 Nm (85 lb-ft); pinch bolts 21 Nm (15 lb-ft).

steps.title: Restore the clickers
steps.instruction: Turn each adjuster in to its stop and back out to the counts you recorded. Refit the number plate and check the fork for leaks after a short ride.

exit_state: Both legs rebuilt and refitted, wheel and brake fitted, clickers back to the recorded settings.

title: Refresh the rear shock spring, eye bearings and seals (sealed damper)
completeness: Covers shock removal and refit, sealed damper inspection, spring and guide inspection, preload, renewal of the upper bearing with its stopper ring and the lower bearing, collar, bushing and dust seals. The damper is a sealed nitrogen unit and is not opened: there is no oil, seal, valving or nitrogen service here.
excluded: Damper oil, seals, piston, valving or nitrogen service (the damper is sealed). A leaking or worn damper goes to a suspension shop for a damper rebuild, or the shock assembly is replaced.

required_tools.name: C-spanner or punch for the shock adjusting nut and locknut
Press or vice with drifts that bear on the outer race only

required_parts.name: Lower dust seals
required_parts.purpose: Renewed whenever the lower bearing is disturbed.

required_parts.name: Lower bearing, upper bearing and stopper ring
Shock assembly
required_parts.purpose: Only if the damper is damaged or leaking and is not being rebuilt by a shop.

prerequisites: No sparks or flames near the open fuel system.
critical_stop_conditions: Oil or gas leaking from the damper, or a bent or scored rod: do not ride; the damper goes to a suspension shop or the shock is replaced. Never open it yourself.
Never heat, puncture or clamp the damper body: it holds high-pressure nitrogen.
Shock eye bore scored or oval: stop; the shock body is damaged.
Bike moves on the stand with the lower bolt out: stop and secure it.
Fuel smell or leak at the hose joint after refit: do not ride until fixed.

steps.title: Record the shock settings
steps.instruction: Count the rebound clicks and the compression settings by turning each adjuster gently in to its stop and back out to where it was; write them down. Measure and record the installed length of the spring on the shock.
verification: Clicker counts and spring length recorded.

steps.title: Lift the rear wheel
steps.instruction: Put the bike on a maintenance stand so the rear wheel is off the ground and the bike cannot tip.
verification: Rear wheel clear of the floor; bike steady.

steps.title: Take off the seat, side covers, air scoops and fuel tank
steps.instruction: Remove the seat, both side covers and both air scoops. Wrap a rag around the fuel hose joint at the tank, release it by hand (slide the cover back and press the two buttons) and cap both ends. Remove the tank and lean it against a wall; never stand it on the fuel pump.
verification: Bodywork and tank off; fuel joint capped.

steps.title: Undo the shock lower mount
steps.instruction: Hold the swingarm up with a block so it cannot drop, then remove the shock lower bolt and pull out the lower bolt.

steps.title: Take the shock out
steps.instruction: Remove the shock upper bolt and bolt and lift the shock out of the frame.

steps.title: Treat the damper as a sealed unit
steps.instruction: The damper body holds high-pressure nitrogen. Never open it, never heat it, and never clamp, dent or deform the body or rod. An old damper being thrown away must have its gas released by a dealer first.
verification: Damper kept away from heat and vice jaws.

steps.title: Inspect the damper
steps.instruction: Clean the shock and look at the rod and body. A bent or damaged rod, or any oil or gas leak, means the damper is finished: a leaking or worn damper goes to a suspension shop for a damper rebuild, or the shock assembly is replaced.
verification: Rod straight and undamaged; no leaks.

branches.label: Damper leaking or damaged
branches.condition: Send the shock to a suspension shop or fit a new assembly; carry on with the spring and bearings on the shock that will go back in.

steps.title: Take the spring off
steps.instruction: Clean the threads, loosen the locknut and wind the adjusting nut back until the spring is free. Remove the lower spring guide, the upper spring guide and the spring.

steps.title: Inspect spring, guides and bolts
steps.instruction: Check the spring for cracks or rub marks, the spring guides for cracks or wear, and both mounting bolts for bends or worn shanks. Replace any damaged part.

steps.title: Check the eye bearings
steps.instruction: Turn the lower bearing with a finger through its collar and check the upper bearing for play or scoring. Any roughness, play, pitting or a torn dust seal means the part and its seals are renewed.

branches.label: Eyes good
branches.condition: No play or roughness and the seals are good.

steps.title: Remove the upper bearing
steps.instruction: Press the upper bearing inward by its outer edge just far enough to free the stopper ring, take the ring out, then press the bearing out.
verification: Upper bearing and stopper ring out.

steps.title: Remove the lower bearing
steps.instruction: Prise out the lower dust seals and take out the collar and bushing. Press the lower bearing out by its outer race only.

steps.title: Grease the new parts
steps.instruction: Grease the lower bearing rollers and the dust seal lips with molybdenum disulfide grease, and the upper O-ring with molybdenum disulfide grease. Keep grease off the outer race of the lower bearing: grease there wears the bore it is pressed into.
verification: Rollers and seal lips greased; outer race clean.

steps.title: Fit the upper bearing
steps.instruction: Press the upper bearing in squarely by its outer edge until the stopper ring groove shows. Fit the stopper ring into the groove, then push the bearing back until it rests against the ring.
verification: Stopper ring fully in its groove.

steps.title: Fit the lower bearing
steps.instruction: Press the lower bearing in by its outer race to an installed depth of 4.25 mm (0.17 in). Fit the bushing and collar, then new dust seals with their lips facing inward.

steps.title: Fit the spring and set preload
steps.instruction: Fit the spring and both spring guides. Wind the adjusting nut in to the installed length you recorded. For the stock setting the spring is shortened 4.0 mm (0.16 in) from its free length; one turn of the adjusting ring changes the length 1.5 mm (0.06 in). Tighten the locknut against the adjusting nut to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Fit the shock
steps.instruction: Grease the shanks and threads of the upper and lower bolts with molybdenum disulfide grease. Lift the swingarm, fit the shock, put the upper bolt in from the right and the lower bolt from the left. Tighten the upper bolt to 56 Nm (41 lb-ft) and the lower bolt to 53 Nm (39 lb-ft).
verification: Upper 56 Nm (41 lb-ft); lower 53 Nm (39 lb-ft).

steps.title: Check the rear moves freely
steps.instruction: Lift and lower the swingarm through its travel by hand: smooth, with no binding or knocking at the shock mounts.

steps.title: Refit the tank and bodywork
steps.instruction: Refit the tank, remove the caps and push the fuel hose joint on until both buttons click; pull on it to prove it is locked. Refit the air scoops, side covers and seat. Start the engine and check for any fuel leak at the joint.

steps.title: Restore settings and bed in
steps.instruction: Set rebound and compression back to the counts you recorded. A new or refreshed shock needs about 50 km (30 miles) of riding to settle; check sag and the mount bolts after the first ride.

title: Service or replace the steering head bearings
completeness: Covers removing the front end, checking and replacing the steering head bearings and races, setting preload and refitting with all torques.

required_parts.name: Upper and lower bearings with races
required_parts.purpose: Only if pitted or rough; always as sets.

critical_stop_conditions: A race will not seat squarely: stop; a cocked race damages the head tube.
Notchy steering after preload is set: the bearings or races are damaged; replace them.

steps.title: Lift the front wheel
steps.instruction: Put the bike on a maintenance stand with the front wheel off the ground and the bike secure.

steps.title: Strip the front end
steps.instruction: Remove the number plate. Remove the front wheel and hang the caliper. Unbolt the handlebar holders and lay the bar back without kinking the cables or hose. Remove the front fender.

steps.title: Remove the stem nut, forks and upper bracket
steps.instruction: Remove the steering stem nut and washer. Support each fork leg, loosen its pinch bolts and slide it out. Lift off the upper bracket.

steps.title: Drop the lower bracket
steps.instruction: Hold the lower bracket so it cannot fall, unscrew the ring nut with the steering nut wrench (Yamaha 90890-01403) and lower the bracket out. Lift off the bearing race cover and the upper bearing.

steps.title: Clean and inspect the bearings
steps.instruction: Wash the bearings and races in solvent. Pitting, rough spots or dents mean new bearings and races; always replace a bearing with its race. Check both brackets and the stem for bends or cracks.

steps.title: Replace the races and lower bearing
steps.instruction: Drive the races out of the steering head with a long drift and hammer, working around evenly. Cut the lower bearing race off the stem with a chisel. Drive the new races in squarely to the bottom of their bores; a crooked race damages the head tube. Fit the new lower bearing on the stem.

steps.title: Grease and assemble
steps.instruction: Grease the lower bearing, its dust seal lip, the upper bearing and the race cover lip with lithium-soap grease, and the stem thread. Fit the lower bracket, the upper bearing and the race cover.

steps.title: Set the bearing preload
steps.instruction: Fit the ring nut with its stepped side down. With the steering nut wrench and a torque wrench at a right angle to it, tighten the nut to 38 Nm (28 lb-ft), turn the bars lock to lock a few times, loosen the nut one full turn and tighten it to 7 Nm (5.2 lb-ft). The stem must turn smoothly with no play.
verification: Ring nut 7 Nm (5.2 lb-ft) after seating at 38 Nm (28 lb-ft).

steps.title: Fit forks and upper bracket
steps.instruction: Fit the washer, forks and upper bracket, snug the lower pinch bolts, grease the stem nut face and tighten the stem nut to 145 Nm (107 lb-ft). Turn the steering lock to lock; if it is tight, back the ring nut off slightly and recheck.

steps.title: Set fork height and pinch bolts
steps.instruction: Set the tops of the fork tubes 7 mm (0.28 in) above the upper bracket, tighten the upper pinch bolts to 21 Nm (15 lb-ft) and the lower to 21 Nm (15 lb-ft).
verification: Pinch bolts 21 Nm (15 lb-ft) / 21 Nm (15 lb-ft).

steps.title: Refit bars, fender and wheel
steps.instruction: Refit the front fender (10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft)), the handlebar (upper holder bolts 28 Nm (21 lb-ft), front bolts first, even gaps; lower holder nuts 40 Nm (30 lb-ft) if removed), the number plate (7 Nm (5.2 lb-ft)), the caliper (28 Nm (21 lb-ft)) and the wheel (axle nut 115 Nm (85 lb-ft), pinch bolts 21 Nm (15 lb-ft)).

steps.title: Check for play
steps.instruction: Grab the bottom of the fork legs and rock them: no knock. Turn the bars: smooth with no notch. Check cables and hoses do not pull at full lock.

title: Service or replace the steering head bearings
completeness: Covers removing the front end, checking and replacing the steering head bearings and races, setting preload and refitting with all torques.

required_parts.name: Upper and lower bearings with races
required_parts.purpose: Only if pitted or rough; always as sets.

critical_stop_conditions: A race will not seat squarely: stop; a cocked race damages the head tube.
Notchy steering after preload is set: the bearings or races are damaged; replace them.

steps.title: Lift the front wheel
steps.instruction: Put the bike on a maintenance stand with the front wheel off the ground and the bike secure.

steps.title: Strip the front end
steps.instruction: Remove the number plate. Remove the front wheel and hang the caliper. Unbolt the handlebar holders and lay the bar back without kinking the cables or hose. Remove the front fender.

steps.title: Remove the stem nut, forks and upper bracket
steps.instruction: Remove the steering stem nut and washer. Support each fork leg, loosen its pinch bolts and slide it out. Lift off the upper bracket.

steps.title: Drop the lower bracket
steps.instruction: Hold the lower bracket so it cannot fall, unscrew the ring nut with the steering nut wrench (Yamaha 90890-01403) and lower the bracket out. Lift off the bearing race cover and the upper bearing.

steps.title: Clean and inspect the bearings
steps.instruction: Wash the bearings and races in solvent. Pitting, rough spots or dents mean new bearings and races; always replace a bearing with its race. Check both brackets and the stem for bends or cracks.

steps.title: Replace the races and lower bearing
steps.instruction: Drive the races out of the steering head with a long drift and hammer, working around evenly. Cut the lower bearing race off the stem with a chisel. Drive the new races in squarely to the bottom of their bores; a crooked race damages the head tube. Fit the new lower bearing on the stem.

steps.title: Grease and assemble
steps.instruction: Grease the lower bearing, its dust seal lip, the upper bearing and the race cover lip with lithium-soap grease, and the stem thread over about 20.0 mm (0.79 in). Fit the lower bracket, the upper bearing and the race cover.

steps.title: Set the bearing preload
steps.instruction: Fit the ring nut with its stepped side down. With the steering nut wrench and a torque wrench at a right angle to it, tighten the nut to 38 Nm (28 lb-ft), turn the bars lock to lock a few times, loosen the nut one full turn and tighten it to 7 Nm (5.2 lb-ft). The stem must turn smoothly with no play.
verification: Ring nut 7 Nm (5.2 lb-ft) after seating at 38 Nm (28 lb-ft).

steps.title: Fit forks and upper bracket
steps.instruction: Fit the washer, forks and upper bracket, snug the lower pinch bolts, grease the stem nut face and tighten the stem nut to 145 Nm (107 lb-ft). Turn the steering lock to lock; if it is tight, back the ring nut off slightly and recheck.

steps.title: Set fork height and pinch bolts
steps.instruction: Set the tops of the fork tubes 5 mm (0.2 in) above the upper bracket, tighten the upper pinch bolts to 21 Nm (15 lb-ft) and the lower to 21 Nm (15 lb-ft).
verification: Pinch bolts 21 Nm (15 lb-ft) / 21 Nm (15 lb-ft).

steps.title: Refit bars, fender and wheel
steps.instruction: Refit the front fender (10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft)), the handlebar (upper holder bolts 28 Nm (21 lb-ft), front bolts first, even gaps; lower holder nuts 40 Nm (30 lb-ft) if removed), the number plate (7 Nm (5.2 lb-ft)), the caliper (28 Nm (21 lb-ft)) and the wheel (axle nut 115 Nm (85 lb-ft), pinch bolts 21 Nm (15 lb-ft)).

steps.title: Check for play
steps.instruction: Grab the bottom of the fork legs and rock them: no knock. Turn the bars: smooth with no notch. Check cables and hoses do not pull at full lock.

exit_state: Steering bearings serviced, preload set, front end refitted.

title: Replace the front and rear wheel bearings and seals
completeness: Covers removing both wheels, checking axles and bearings, replacing all wheel bearings, the rear circlip and the seals, and refitting with axle and chain settings.

required_tools.name: Sockets to drive bearings by the outer race

critical_stop_conditions: A bent axle: replace it.
A bearing bore loose in the hub: stop; the hub is damaged.

steps.title: Remove the front wheel
steps.instruction: With the front wheel off the ground, loosen the axle pinch bolts, remove the axle nut and pull the axle. Lower the wheel out and take off the collars.

steps.title: Check the front axle and bearings
steps.instruction: Roll the axle on a flat surface; never straighten a bent axle (bend limit 0.50 mm (0.02 in)). Turn each bearing with a finger: roughness or play means new bearings and seals.

steps.title: Remove the front bearings
steps.instruction: Clean the hub. Lever the seals out with a flat screwdriver over a rag. Pull the bearings with a bearing puller and take out the spacer.

steps.title: Fit new front bearings
steps.instruction: Press the left bearing in first, square, with a socket on its outer race only. Fit the spacer, then press in the right bearing. Fit new seals with their marks facing out, and grease the seal lips with lithium grease. Refit the collars.

steps.title: Refit the front wheel
steps.instruction: Fit the wheel with the disc between the pads, grease the axle, pump the fork and tighten the axle nut to 115 Nm (85 lb-ft) and the pinch bolts to 21 Nm (15 lb-ft). Pump the brake lever firm.
verification: Axle nut 115 Nm (85 lb-ft); pinch 21 Nm (15 lb-ft).

steps.title: Remove the rear wheel
steps.instruction: With the rear wheel off the ground, remove the axle nut, loosen the puller locknuts and turn the adjusting bolts in, push the wheel forward, lift the chain off, pull the axle and roll the wheel out. Do not press the brake pedal. Take off the collars.

steps.title: Remove the rear bearings
steps.instruction: Lever out both seals. The brake disc side has one bearing held by a circlip; the sprocket side has two bearings. Remove the circlip, pull all three bearings with a bearing puller and take out the spacer.

steps.title: Fit new rear bearings
steps.instruction: Press the disc-side bearing in first by its outer race and fit a new circlip. Fit the spacer, then press in the two sprocket-side bearings. Fit new seals with marks facing out, and grease the seal lips. Refit the collars. If the sprocket or disc was removed: sprocket nuts 42 Nm (31 lb-ft) in a crisscross, disc bolts 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft) with threadlocker.

steps.title: Refit the rear wheel
steps.instruction: Fit the wheel with the disc between the pads, loop the chain on, fit the left puller and push the greased axle in from the left, then the right puller, washer and nut finger tight. Set chain slack to 50.0–60.0 mm (1.97–2.36 in) on the stand, tighten the axle nut to 135 Nm (100 lb-ft) and the locknuts to 21 Nm (15 lb-ft). Pump the brake pedal firm.
verification: Axle nut 135 Nm (100 lb-ft); slack 50.0–60.0 mm (1.97–2.36 in).

steps.title: Spin check
steps.instruction: Spin both wheels: they must turn freely and quietly with no side play, and the brakes must work.

exit_state: New wheel bearings and seals in both wheels; wheels refitted and torqued.
